issue.title: Persist ToolRun finish diagnostics in sase-core so a settled run can explain its own failure
issue.description:
`sase tool run` computes several typed diagnostics that never become durable, because `canonical_event` in sase-core strips the `diagnostics` field and `tool_run_finish` stores none of its own:

- the typed spawn-failure reason (executable not found vs. present but not executable) behind exit 127 / 126,
- stage-ingest diagnostics from reading a torn or malformed `events.jsonl`,
- log-write facts (which retained log could not be written, and why).

All three are printed to the operator at the time of the run and then lost. `sase tool show RUN` and `sase tool show RUN -j` on a settled run report the exit facts but cannot explain them, which is exactly the reconstruction the ledger exists to provide. Phase 7 worked around the log case narrowly by recording truncation as an output record in `events.jsonl` (`logs.record_truncation`); that is a point fix, not the general contract.

Proposed by phase bead sase-135.7 (epic sase-135) as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note; filed by the sase-135 land agent on 2026-09-20. Out of scope for the epic because the V1 wire deliberately froze `schema_version: 1` once phase 1 landed, and persisting diagnostics changes the stored record shape in sase-core rather than the Python presentation layer this phase owned.

task_type_fields.proposal: Give ToolRun finish a durable diagnostics channel in ../sase-core/crates/sase_core/src/tool_run/ so the typed spawn-failure reason, stage-ingest diagnostics, and log-write facts survive on the stored record and surface through sase tool show / show -j, instead of being printed once and discarded by canonical_event.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: It changes the sase-core V1 stored record and wire shape, which phase 1 of epic sase-135 deliberately froze at schema_version 1 before the later phases discovered these diagnostics; phase 7 could only work around the log case locally (logs.record_truncation in events.jsonl).
